difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. Stimulus: price increase caused lower sales. Correct answer introduces a confounding variable (competitor entered market) that provides an obvious alternative cause.
stimulus: In the past year, the widget division of Acme Corporation reduced production by 20% immediately after implementing a 15% price increase on its main product. Company executives concluded that the price increase caused the reduction in sales. The reduction forced the company to scale back manufacturing, explaining the 20% drop in production volume.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acme Corporation's widget division had reduced production in previous years without implementing price increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major competitor launched a heavily marketed new widget product in the same month the price increase took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The widget division's profit margin increased despite the reduction in sales volume.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most industries experience some fluctuation in sales volume year to year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acme Corporation's other product divisions did not implement price increases during the same period.

explanations.correct: If a competitor launched a new product around the same time as the price increase, the sales decline could be explained by lost market share to the competitor rather than by the price increase itself. This alternative explanation undermines the conclusion that the price increase caused the sales reduction.
explanations.A: While this shows production reductions occurred before, it does not explain away the current decline or suggest an alternative cause for this year's reduction. It's consistent with price increases being the cause this time.
explanations.B: Correct. This provides a plausible competing explanation for the sales drop.
explanations.C: Increased profit margins despite lower volume may actually support the price increase as beneficial, rather than weakening the argument that it caused the decline.
explanations.D: This generic fact about industry volatility does not explain this specific sales drop or suggest the price increase was not the cause.
explanations.E: What other divisions did is irrelevant to whether the price increase caused the widget division's sales decline.

difficultyReason: Simple predictive argument with one obvious confounding variable. Stimulus claims a museum's free-admission policy caused increased attendance. Correct answer shows attendance rose for a separate, independent reason.
stimulus: The City Museum implemented a new free-admission policy last month. Since the policy's introduction, attendance at the museum has increased by 35%. The director credits the free-admission policy with driving this increase in visitors, arguing that removing the price barrier has made the museum more accessible to the public.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Other museums in the city do not charge admission fees.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The museum had introduced several new exhibits featuring renowned artwork during the same month the free-admission policy took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free-admission policies typically increase attendance at cultural institutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The museum's operating costs increased after implementing the free-admission policy.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surveys show that price is an important factor in people's decisions about museum attendance.

explanations.correct: If new exhibits featuring renowned artwork were introduced in the same month as the free-admission policy, the attendance increase could be attributed to the new exhibits rather than the removal of admission fees. This provides an alternative explanation for the 35% rise in visitors.
explanations.A: What other museums charge is irrelevant to why this museum's attendance increased.
explanations.B: Correct. This offers a competing explanation for the attendance surge.
explanations.C: This actually strengthens the argument by confirming that free policies generally drive attendance.
explanations.D: Cost increases to the museum do not explain why attendance went up; this is about the museum's finances, not visitor motivation.
explanations.E: This would support the argument that the price barrier removal drove the increase; it strengthens rather than weakens.

difficultyReason: Straightforward analogical argument where the conclusion overreaches similarity between two cases. Stimulus claims one technology will succeed because a similar technology succeeded. Correct answer reveals a disanalogy that breaks the analogy.
stimulus: The transition to hybrid vehicles in the automotive market succeeded because consumers recognized both environmental and financial benefits. Smartphone manufacturers should have equal success transitioning consumers to foldable phones, since foldable phones offer similar technological advantages and aesthetic benefits. Thus, the foldable phone transition will follow the same successful trajectory as the hybrid vehicle transition.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Foldable phones currently have a higher price point than most conventional smartphones.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hybrid vehicles require relatively minimal changes to driving habits and infrastructure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some early adopters of hybrid vehicles reported experiencing mechanical problems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Foldable phones have been available to consumers for several years now.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smartphone manufacturers have successfully introduced other technological innovations in the past.

explanations.correct: The argument assumes that because both offer 'technological and aesthetic benefits,' they will succeed similarly. However, a critical disanalogy emerges: hybrid vehicles required minimal changes to infrastructure and habit, while foldable phones—if they require new behaviors or ecosystem adjustments—present a different adoption barrier. This breaks the analogy and weakens the conclusion.
explanations.A: A price premium could explain slower adoption, but this is compatible with eventual success, so it only moderately weakens. (B) is more direct.
explanations.B: Correct. This highlights a key difference: hybrids fit seamlessly into existing driving patterns, whereas foldable phones might require greater behavioral changes, breaking the analogy.
explanations.C: Early mechanical problems plagued hybrids too; this is not a disanalogy.
explanations.D: The availability timeline doesn't explain why the adoption trajectories differ or strengthen the analogy.
explanations.E: Past innovation success doesn't guarantee the foldable phone will follow the hybrid path, and doesn't address the analogy.
